sentences: While stuck in the city's traffic (a song), a jazz pianist has a moment of road rage directed at an aspiring actress.
After a hard day at work, the actress's next audition goes awry because the casting director takes a phone call during an emotional scene.
That night, her roommates take her to a lavish party in the hills, promising her that it could jump-start her career (a song).
After her car is towed, she walks home in disappointment.
During a gig at a restaurant, the pianist slips into jazz improvisation despite the owner's warning to only play traditional Christmas pieces.
The actress hears him playing as she passes by.
Moved, she enters the restaurant and observes the pianist being fired for his disobedience.
The actress attempts to compliment him as he storms out, but he roughly shoulders past her.
Months later, she runs into the pianist at a party where he plays in a 1980s pop cover band.
The actress requests that the pianist play a song for her.
After the gig, they walk to their cars and lament wasting the night on each other (a song), despite their clear chemistry.
The pianist arrives at the cafe where the actress works, and she shows him around a studio backlot while expressing her passion for movies and acting.
He takes her to a jazz club, where he shares his passion for jazz and his dream to open his own jazz club.
The pianist invites the actress to a screening of a film (1955) and she accepts.
The actress later remembers a conflicting dinner date with her boyfriend, and initially forgoes the movie to go on the original date.
However, finding herself bored with the date, she rushes to the theater and finds the pianist just as the film begins.
When the screening is interrupted by a projector malfunction, the pianist and the actress spend the rest of the evening together with a romantic visit to the observatory, where they share a kiss.
After more failed auditions, the actress decides, with the pianist's encouragement, to write a one-woman play.
The pianist begins to perform regularly at a jazz club, and the two of them eventually move in together (a song).
A former bandmate of the pianist's invites him to be the keyboardist in a new jazz pop band, which will give him a steady income.
Although dismayed by the band's pop style, the pianist signs on after hearing the actress trying to convince her mother that he is working on his career.
The band finds success, but the actress knows their music is not the type of music the pianist wants to perform (a song).
During the band's first tour, the pianist and the actress argue.
She accuses him of abandoning his dreams, while he insists that she liked him more when he was unsuccessful because it made her feel better about herself.
Two weeks later, the pianist misses the actress's play because of a photoshoot he had forgotten about.
The play fails, very few people attend, and the actress overhears dismissive comments about her performance.
Unable to forgive the pianist for missing her play and for their previous argument, the actress breaks up with the pianist and returns to her hometown.
The pianist receives a call from a prominent casting director who attended the actress's play, inviting her to audition for an upcoming film.
Knowing that this could be her big break, he drives in a hurry to her hometown to tell the actress.
He successfully finds her house by recalling that she lived across the street from the library, where she first fell in love with acting.
The pianist persuades her to attend, and she reluctantly agrees to go.
During the audition the next day, the actress is asked to tell a story.
In response, she sings about how her aunt, a one-time stage actress who eventually died from alcoholism, inspired her to chase her dreams (a song).
Confident the audition was a success, the pianist encourages the actress to devote herself to acting.
The two recognize that they will always love each other despite what may come for their relationship.
Five years later, the actress is living a happy life as a successful actress and married to a different man, with whom she has a daughter.
That night, the couple stumble upon a jazz bar.
Recognizing the logo she had once designed, the actress realizes that the pianist has opened his own jazz club.
The pianist notices the actress in the crowd so plays their love theme on the piano.
The two imagine what their happy life together would have been (a song) had their relationship thrived along with their careers, then acknowledge each other with a silent exchange of smiles.
On their fifth anniversary, a writing teacher returns home to find that his wife is missing.
The wife's fame as the inspiration for her parents' children's books ensures widespread press coverage.
The media finds the husband's apathy towards the disappearance suspicious.
Before her disappearance, the couple's marriage deteriorated.
Both lost their jobs in the recession and moved from the city to the husband's hometown to support his dying mother.
The husband grew distant from the wife and began an affair with his student, while the wife became resentful toward the husband.
A detective and the forensic team find evidence of a struggle and blood loss in the house.
The detective learns of the couple's financial problems, disputes, and the wife's attempt to buy a gun.
Medical reports indicate that the wife was pregnant, of which the husband denies knowledge.
On each anniversary, the wife sets up elaborate treasure hunts for the husband.
This year's clues appear in places where the husband had sex with the student, revealing the wife's knowledge of his affair.
The husband discovers thousands of dollars' worth of items purchased with his credit card, unauthorized and hidden in his sister's woodshed.
The wife's clues lead authorities to a diary documenting her growing fear that the husband will kill her.
The wife hides in a campground in the hills.
After discovering the husband's affair, the wife conceived an elaborate plan to frame him for her murder.

She had him increase her life insurance, secretly used his credit card to buy the woodshed items, stole a sample of her pregnant neighbor's urine to fake a pregnancy to elicit media sympathy, wrote increasingly fabricated diary entries and placed incriminating evidence for police to find.
On the morning of her disappearance, the wife drained and splattered her own blood across the kitchen.
Her original plan was to drown herself after the husband's arrest and have her body found to ensure his death sentence.
The husband deduces the wife's scheme, convinces his sister of his innocence, and hires a lawyer known for representing husbands suspected of uxoricide.
The husband meets two of the wife's ex-boyfriends.
The first claims that she framed him for rape and ruined his life after they broke up.
The wealthy second ex-boyfriend, against whom the wife filed a restraining order for stalking, rejects the husband.
When the wife's campground neighbors rob her, she calls the wealthy ex-boyfriend for help, convincing him that she fled the husband's abuse.
The ex-boyfriend agrees to hide her in his lakehouse.
The lawyer convinces the husband to admit to his affair on a popular talk show, thus seizing the narrative initiative from the media.
The student reveals the affair at a press conference shortly beforehand, but the husband insists on conducting the interview.
He affirms his innocence and feigns regret for his shortcomings as a spouse, knowing that the wife is watching.
The interview garners widespread sympathy for the husband.
However, the detective, having gathered adequate evidence, arrests the husband and his sister.
The lawyer bails them out, and they brace for the impending trial.
After watching the husband's interview, the wife rekindles her attraction to him and begins crafting her escape story.
Using surveillance cameras and self-inflicted injuries, she makes it appear that the ex-boyfriend kidnapped and raped her.
She seduces the ex-boyfriend, slits his throat during sex, and returns home, clearing the husband of suspicion.
Medical examiners lend credence to the wife's story.
During questioning, the detective probes her inconsistencies, but the wife accuses the detective of incompetence.
Federal investigators close the case, but the detective gleans the wife's guilt.
At home, the wife tells the husband the truth, but says that she forgives him after seeing him plead for her return on TV.
The husband shares this with the detective, the lawyer, and his sister.
They agree that the wife is guilty, but acknowledge a lack of evidence.
The lawyer wishes the husband well and returns to the city.
A young federal trainee at the academy is recruited by a unit chief to interview a brilliant and cannibalistic psychiatrist imprisoned at a state hospital for the criminally insane.
Officially conducting a psychological survey, the trainee is actually meant to draw out insights that could help capture a serial killer who murders young women and removes their skin.
At the hospital, the director makes unwelcome advances toward the trainee before escorting her to the psychiatrist's cell.
Initially courteous, the psychiatrist grows dismissive upon deducing the unit chief's ulterior motive.
As the trainee departs, an inmate flings semen at her, provoking the psychiatrist's ire.

He summons her back and offers an anagram as a clue that leads her to a storage unit containing a severed head in a jar—later revealed to belong to a former patient of the psychiatrist whose killer is believed to be the serial killer.
Soon afterward, the inmate is found dead, having swallowed his own tongue—orchestrated by the psychiatrist as retribution.
The psychiatrist agrees to assist in exchange for a transfer away from the director.
Meanwhile, another victim is discovered with a death's-head moth lodged in her throat—the same species later found inside the severed head.
When the serial killer abducts the daughter of a senator, the unit chief authorizes the trainee to offer the psychiatrist a fraudulent deal: a prison transfer in return for actionable intelligence.
The psychiatrist instead demands a quid pro quo, extracting personal details from the trainee, who reveals that her father, a police officer, was murdered when she was ten, leaving her orphaned.

In exchange, the psychiatrist reveals that the serial killer is not a genuine transsexual but mistakenly believes he is, having possibly been rejected from gender-reassignment clinics due to psychological instability.
The director secretly records the conversation, exposes her deceit, and offers the psychiatrist relocation in exchange for information.
The psychiatrist complies and is flown to another city, where he provides the senator with accurate details about the serial killer's appearance but falsely identifies him by a false name.
Meanwhile, the serial killer holds the senator's daughter captive in a dry well in his basement, demanding she apply lotion to her skin; the daughter manages to seize his dog as leverage.
The trainee deciphers the false name as an anagram for "iron sulfide" (fool's gold) and confronts the psychiatrist in his temporary cell at a courthouse.

The psychiatrist demands deeper revelations and offers a clue—"we covet what we see every day"—before the trainee recounts a traumatic childhood incident: after her father's death, she lived on a relative's farm, where she failed to save spring lambs from slaughter.
The psychiatrist intuits that saving the senator's daughter might silence this recurring trauma and, satisfied, returns the case files.
That night, he uses a piece of the director's pen to unlock his restraints, murders two guards, and escapes in an ambulance disguised in a dead guard's uniform and skinned face.
Analyzing the psychiatrist's annotations, the trainee deduces that the serial killer knew his first victim, a tailor, and follows the lead.

At the first victim's home, she finds unfinished dresses and patterns matching patches of skin removed from the victims, realizing the killer seeks to construct a "suit" of human flesh and starves his plump captives to loosen their skin.

The unit chief cross-references the psychiatrist's profile with names from a hospital and a known-offenders database, identifying a man as the prime suspect; the name is confirmed through airport customs papers listing the suspect as the addressee of live death's-head moth caterpillars imported from abroad.
While the unit chief's team raids the suspect's vacant residence, the trainee interviews the first victim's acquaintances and arrives at a house where the suspect poses under another name.
His façade crumbles when the trainee spots a death's-head moth.
Pursuing the suspect into his basement, the trainee discovers the senator's daughter trapped in the well.
The suspect stalks the trainee in complete darkness using night-vision goggles, but betrays his position by cocking his revolver; the trainee fires instinctively and kills him.
The senator's daughter is rescued.
The trainee graduates from the academy.
During the post-ceremony party, the psychiatrist calls from an unnamed location, asking whether "the lambs have stopped screaming."
He assures her he has no intention of pursuing her and asks that she return the favor—a request she declines.
The psychiatrist announces he is "having an old friend for dinner" before stalking the director into a crowd.
In 1987, a man is the executive sales manager of a car dealership in the city owned by his father-in-law.
Desperate for money, the sales manager plans to have his wife kidnapped.
On the recommendation of a dealership mechanic and parolee, the sales manager meets two criminals at a bar in another town.
The two criminals agree to kidnap the wife in exchange for a new car and half of the $80,000 ransom the sales manager intends to extort from his father-in-law.
Believing he has secured a $750,000 loan from his father-in-law for a lucrative real estate deal, the sales manager unsuccessfully tries to call off the kidnapping.
The father-in-law and his accountant inform the sales manager that they never intended the sales manager to handle the $750,000 deal, offering him only a modest finder's fee.
The criminal and his accomplice kidnap the wife and transport her to a remote cabin in another town.
A state trooper stops them near a town for not displaying temporary registration tags on the new car.
The trooper rejects the criminal's clumsy bribe attempt and orders the criminal out of the car.
When the trooper hears the wife whimpering in the back seat, the accomplice shoots him dead, then hunts down and kills two passersby who witnessed the scene.
The local police chief, who is seven months pregnant, begins investigating.
She correctly infers that the dead trooper was ticketing a car with dealer plates.
She later learns that two men driving a dealership vehicle checked into a nearby motel with two call girls and placed a call to the mechanic.
The police chief visits the father-in-law's dealership, where the mechanic feigns ignorance and the sales manager nervously insists no cars are missing.
While in the city, the police chief reconnects with a high school classmate, who awkwardly tries to romance the police chief before breaking down, saying that his wife has died and he is lonely.
The sales manager tells his father-in-law the kidnappers have demanded $1 million and will deal only through him.
In light of the three murders, the criminal demands that the sales manager hand over the $80,000 he believes is the entire ransom.
The mechanic finds the criminal with a call girl in the mechanic's city apartment and beats him in retaliation for bringing the mechanic to the police's attention.
The criminal angrily calls the sales manager and demands that he bring the money immediately.
The father-in-law insists on delivering the ransom and meets the criminal at a parking garage.
The father-in-law refuses to hand over the money without seeing his daughter, so the criminal shoots him.
The father-in-law fires back, wounding the criminal in the jaw.
The criminal kills the father-in-law and a garage attendant, then drives away with the ransom.
On the way to the cabin, the criminal discovers the briefcase contains $1 million.
He takes out $80,000 to split with his accomplice and buries the rest in the snow alongside the highway.
The police chief learns from a friend that the classmate does not have a wife and is mentally ill.

Reflecting on the lies, the police chief returns to the father-in-law's dealership, where an agitated sales manager again insists no cars are missing and tells the police chief he will double-check the inventory.
The police chief sees the sales manager driving off the lot and calls the state police.
At the cabin, the criminal finds that his accomplice killed the wife because she would not stay quiet.
The criminal says they should split up and leave immediately, and they argue over who will keep the car.
The criminal insults his accomplice and attempts to leave with the car, but the accomplice kills him with an axe.
The police chief drives to the town, tipped off by a local bartender who overheard a customer brag about killing someone.
She sees the car, then discovers the accomplice feeding the criminal's body into a woodchipper.
The accomplice attempts to flee, but the police chief shoots him in the leg and arrests him.
Shortly after, the sales manager is arrested by state troopers at a motel outside another city.

The police chief's husband tells her the postal service has selected his painting of a mallard for a 3-cent postage stamp and complains that a painting by two brothers won the competition for a 29-cent stamp.
The police chief reminds him that smaller denomination stamps make up the difference between the face value of old stamps and the new cost of first-class postage.
Her husband is reassured, and the couple happily anticipates the birth of their child.
In 1937, in the city, a woman identifying herself as the engineer's wife hires a private investigator
to trail her husband, the chief engineer at the water department.
The detective photographs the engineer in the company of a young woman and the pictures make their way into the newspaper, exposing their apparent affair.
The detective is then confronted by the real wife, who threatens to sue him.
He concludes that the impostor was using him to discredit the engineer.
The detective crosses paths with his former colleague, a police lieutenant, when the engineer's corpse is found in a reservoir.
Investigating further, he discovers that huge quantities of water are being released from the reservoir each night, despite the fact that the city is in the midst of a drought.
The water department's security chief warns him off, and he has his nose slashed by one of the security chief's henchmen.
The detective receives a call from the woman who posed as the wife.
She refuses to say who hired her, but urges the detective to check the newspaper's obituary section.
Now working for the wife, the detective investigates the engineer's death.
He learns that the engineer was once the business partner of the wife's wealthy father.
The father offers to double the detective's fee if he finds the engineer's supposed mistress, who has disappeared.
Public records reveal that much of the valley has recently changed ownership.
The detective recognizes one of the buyers' names from the obituary section; the obituary indicates that he had been dead for a week when the deal was closed.

The detective and the wife bluff their way into the retirement home where the buyer had lived and discover that many of the other residents are "buyers" too, although they have no knowledge of this fact.
A suspicious staff member calls the security chief, but the detective and the wife escape him and his thugs and hide at her mansion, where they sleep together.
Later that night, the detective follows the wife to a house where he sees her comforting the missing girl.
When confronted, the wife claims the girl is her sister.
A call from the lieutenant summons the detective to the impostor's apartment; she has been murdered.
The lieutenant reveals that the engineer had saltwater in his lungs, indicating that he did not drown in the reservoir.
He suspects the wife is responsible for her husband's murder and tells the detective to produce her quickly.
At the engineer's residence, the detective retrieves a pair of bifocals from the saltwater garden pond.
The detective confronts the wife about both the girl, who she now claims is her daughter, and her husband, whom she denies murdering.

Frustrated, he repeatedly slaps the wife until she breaks down and reveals that the girl is both her sister and daughter; the girl's father is the wife's own father, who impregnated her when she was 15.
She tells the detective that the glasses he found did not belong to the engineer, because he did not wear bifocals.
The detective arranges for the women to flee abroad and instructs the wife to meet him at her butler's home in the district.
He summons the father to the engineer's estate, having deduced that the father dropped his bifocals when he drowned the engineer in the pond.
The father reveals that he is behind both the water shortage and the land grab in the valley.
Once the land is his, he will obtain a contract from the city to build a reservoir there.
He discredited and killed the engineer when the latter came close to uncovering the scheme.
The father has the security chief take the glasses from the detective at gunpoint.
The detective is then forced to drive them to the rendezvous in the district, where the police are waiting.
The lieutenant detains the detective as the father attempts to claim the girl.
The wife shoots the father in the arm and tries to escape with the girl, but the police open fire, killing her.
The father takes a distraught girl away, and the lieutenant orders the detective released.
As the detective is led away by his associates, one tells him, "Forget it, detective.
It's the district."
A professional thief in the city and his crew—three crew members and a new recruit—rob $1.6 million in bearer bonds from an armored car.
The new recruit, who unbeknownst to the thief is an active serial killer who targets underaged prostitutes, kills a guard without provocation, forcing the crew to kill two other guards.
The thief plans to kill the new recruit in retribution for the guards' deaths, but the new recruit escapes.
A police robbery-homicide detective lieutenant and his team investigate the robbery.
The detective, a dedicated lawman and former marine, has a strained relationship with his third wife, and struggles to connect with his stepdaughter.
The thief, who lives a solitary life, begins a relationship with a graphic designer who is new to the city and has no local connections.
The thief's fence suggests selling the stolen bonds to their original owner, a money launderer.
The launderer pretends to agree, but instead arranges an ambush.
Anticipating a trap, the thief and his crew counter-ambush and kill the hitmen.
Afterward, the thief threatens to kill the launderer.
An informant connects the second crew member to the robbery, and the detective's team begins monitoring him, identifying the rest of the crew and their next target, a precious metals depository.
The team stakes out the depository and subsequently breaks in, but when a careless officer makes a noise, the thief aborts the heist.
Unable to prove the thief's crew stole anything, the detective reluctantly lets them escape.
The next day, the thief's crew plans one final bank robbery worth $12.2 million.
The detective stops the thief on the freeway and invites him to coffee.
They discuss their dedication to their jobs and personal limitations.
The detective talks about his failing marriage, and the thief admits he is also isolated.
Both men express mutual respect, but declare they will kill the other if necessary.
The new recruit makes a deal with the launderer to eliminate the thief's crew.
The third crew member backs out of the heist after suspecting he is being monitored by the police.
The thief hires an old colleague as the getaway driver, and they execute the heist.
Tipped by the launderer's associate, the police intercept the crew after leaving the bank, sparking a shootout.
The getaway driver and the second crew member, along with many police, are killed, while the first crew member is wounded.
The thief and the first crew member escape, and the thief takes the first crew member to a doctor before leaving him with the fence.
Suspecting the third crew member tipped off the police, the thief goes to his house to find him mortally wounded and his wife dead.
Before asking the thief to kill him, the third crew member reveals the new recruit and the launderer were responsible and forced him to disclose the bank heist.
The thief kills the launderer at his home, while the detective's team detains the associate.
Discovering the thief's connection to the new recruit, who is hiding in a hotel, the detective uses the new recruit as bait to lure the thief.
As the thief plans to retreat, the designer discovers his criminal identity but agrees to go with him.
The first crew member plans to reconcile with his estranged wife, who is being forced by the police to bring him in.
When the first crew member arrives at his wife's safe house, she warns him off with a hand gesture and he escapes.
Having separated from his wife, the detective finds his stepdaughter in his hotel room, unconscious after attempting suicide.
He rushes her to the hospital and saves her life.
The detective reconciles with his wife, although the two agree that their marriage will never work.
The thief drives with the designer to the city's international airport to flee abroad via private jet.
However, when the fence gives him the new recruit's location, the thief abandons his usual caution to seek revenge.
Posing as hotel security and triggering a fire alarm evacuation, the thief infiltrates the hotel and kills the new recruit in his room.
However, as the thief returns to the designer, he is spotted by the detective and flees.
The detective chases the thief onto the tarmac at the airport, and the two stalk each other before the detective gets the upper hand and shoots the thief.
The detective takes the thief's hand as he dies of his wounds.
On Christmas Eve, an out-of-town police detective arrives in the city, hoping to reconcile with his estranged wife at a party held by her employer, a corporation.
He is driven to the company's tower by a limo driver, who offers to wait for the detective in the garage.
While the detective washes himself, the tower is seized by an ex-radical and his heavily armed team, including two gunmen.
Everyone in the tower is taken hostage except for the detective, who slips away, and the limo driver, who remains oblivious to events.
The ex-radical is posing as a terrorist to steal the $640 million in untraceable bearer bonds in the building's vault.
He kills an executive after failing to extract the access code from him and tasks the second gunman with breaking into the vault.
The terrorists are alerted to the detective's presence, and the first gunman's brother is sent after him.
The detective kills the brother and takes his weapon and radio, which he uses to contact the skeptical local police department.
A police sergeant is sent to investigate.
Meanwhile, the detective kills more terrorists and recovers their bag of C-4 and detonators.
Realizing the sergeant is about to leave, having found nothing amiss, the detective drops a terrorist's corpse onto his car.
After the sergeant calls for backup, a SWAT team attempts to storm the building but is counterattacked by the terrorists.
The detective throws some C-4 down an elevator shaft, causing an explosion that kills some of the terrorists and ends the counterattack.
The wife's co-worker attempts to negotiate on the ex-radical's behalf but is killed by the ex-radical when the detective refuses to surrender.
While checking the explosives on the roof, the ex-radical encounters the detective and pretends to be an escaped hostage; the detective gives the ex-radical a gun.
The ex-radical attempts to shoot the detective but finds the weapon is unloaded, and he is saved only by the intervention of other terrorists.
The detective escapes but is injured by shattered glass and loses the detonators.
Outside, federal agents take control.
They order the power to be shut off, which, as the ex-radical had anticipated, disables the final vault lock so his team can collect the bonds.
The federal agents agree to the ex-radical's demand for a helicopter, intending to send helicopter gunships to eliminate the group.
The detective realizes the ex-radical plans to blow the roof to kill the hostages and fake his team's deaths.
The first gunman, enraged by his brother's death, attacks the detective and is seemingly killed.
The ex-radical sees a news report by a reporter on the detective's children and infers that he is the wife's husband.
The hostages are taken to the roof while the ex-radical keeps the wife with him.
The detective drives the hostages from the roof just before the ex-radical detonates it and destroys the approaching federal helicopters.
Meanwhile, the second gunman retrieves an escape vehicle from the parking garage but is knocked out by the limo driver, who has been following events on the limo's CB radio.
A weary and battered detective finds his wife with the ex-radical and his remaining henchman.

The detective seemingly surrenders to the ex-radical and is about to be shot but grabs his concealed service pistol taped to his back and uses his last two bullets to wound the ex-radical and kill his accomplice.
The ex-radical crashes through a window but grabs onto the wife's wristwatch and makes a last-ditch attempt to kill the pair.
The detective unclasps the watch, and the ex-radical falls to his death.
Outside, the first gunman ambushes the detective and his wife, only to be shot dead by the sergeant.
The wife punches the reporter when he attempts to interview the detective.
The limo driver crashes through the parking garage door in the limo and drives the detective and his wife away together.
In 1936, an archaeologist recovers a golden idol from a booby-trapped temple.
A rival archaeologist corners him and steals the idol; the archaeologist escapes in a waiting float plane.

After returning home, the archaeologist is briefed by two army intelligence agents that enemy forces have discovered and are excavating at a site abroad, and one of their telegrams mentions the archaeologist's former mentor.
He deduces that the enemy is seeking an ark, which their leader believes will render their army invincible.
The agents recruit the archaeologist to recover the ark first.
At a bar abroad, the archaeologist reunites with the mentor's daughter, with whom he once had an illicit relationship, and learns that the mentor is dead.
The bar is set ablaze during a shootout with a secret police agent and his men, who arrive to take a medallion from the daughter.
The secret police agent attempts to recover the medallion from the flames but only burns its image into his hand.
The archaeologist and the daughter take the medallion and escape.

Traveling to another city, the pair meet the archaeologist's friend, who reveals that the rival is assisting the enemy and that they have fashioned an incomplete replica medallion from the image burned into the secret police agent's hand.
Enemy soldiers and mercenaries attack the archaeologist, and the daughter is seemingly killed, leaving him despondent.

An imam deciphers the medallion for the archaeologist, revealing that one side bears a warning against disturbing the ark and the other—which the enemy does not possess—contains a correction to the measurements for the staff, which, when combined with the medallion, is used to locate the ark.

The archaeologist and his friend realize the enemy is digging in the wrong location, infiltrate the dig site, and use the medallion and a correctly sized staff to locate a well, the ark's resting place.
They recover the ark, a golden, intricately decorated chest, but the rival and the enemy discover them and seize it.
The archaeologist and the daughter, whom the rival has been holding captive, are sealed inside the well, but they escape, and the archaeologist captures a truck carrying the ark.
Alongside the daughter, the archaeologist arranges to transport the ark overseas aboard a tramp steamer.
An enemy U-boat intercepts them, seizing the ark and the daughter; the archaeologist covertly boards the U-boat.
The vessel travels to an island at sea, where the rival intends to test the power of the ark before presenting it to the enemy's leader.
On the island, the archaeologist ambushes the enemy group and threatens to destroy the ark.
He surrenders after the rival deduces that he would never destroy something so historically significant and also surmising that the archaeologist wants to know if the ark's power is real.
The enemy soldiers restrain the archaeologist and the daughter at the testing site as the rival ceremonially opens the ark but finds only sand inside.

At the archaeologist's instruction, he and the daughter close their eyes to avoid looking at the opened ark, as it releases spirits, flames, and bolts of energy that kill the rival, the secret police agent, and the assembled enemy soldiers before sealing itself shut.
The archaeologist and the daughter open their eyes to find the area cleared of bodies and their bindings gone.
Back in the capital, the government rewards the archaeologist for securing the ark.
Despite the archaeologist's questioning, the agents state only that the ark has been moved to an undisclosed location for "top men" to study.
In a vast warehouse, the ark is crated up and stored among countless other crates.
A girl lives on a farm with her uncle and aunt.
Her dog is seized by a neighbor, who has obtained a sheriff's order after being bitten by him.
The dog escapes and returns to the girl, who runs away to protect him.
A charlatan fortune teller leads the girl to believe that her aunt is sick with heartbreak, which prompts the girl to return home.
She returns just as a tornado approaches the farm.
Unable to get into the locked storm cellar, she takes cover in the farmhouse and is knocked unconscious by a blown out window while inside.
She seemingly awakens to find the house moving through the air, with her and the dog still inside it.
Various figures float by, including the neighbor, who morphs into a witch.
The house comes down in an unknown land, which turns out to be a region of a larger realm.
The girl is greeted by a good witch, who comes down in a bubble and informs her that the house landed on a wicked witch, killing her.
The inhabitants celebrate the witch's death, until her sister, another wicked witch, shows up.
Before she can seize her deceased sister's ruby slippers, the good witch magically transports them onto the girl's feet and tells her to keep them on.
The wicked witch leaves, but swears vengeance upon the girl and the dog.
The good witch, before vanishing out of sight in another bubble, tells the girl that the wizard in the city is the only one who might be able to help her return home.
The girl sets out down the yellow brick road to see him.
Along the way, the girl meets a scarecrow, who wants a brain; a tin man, who wants a heart; and a lion, who wants courage.
They join the girl, hoping that the wizard can help them as well.
They reach the city, despite the efforts of the wicked witch.
The wizard appears as a giant ghostly head and tells them he will grant their wishes if they bring him the wicked witch's broom.
During their quest, the girl and the dog are captured by flying monkeys and taken to the wicked witch's castle.
The dog escapes, and leads the scarecrow, tin man, and lion to the castle.
They free the girl, but are pursued and finally cornered by the witch and her guards.
She taunts them and sets fire to the scarecrow's arm.
When the girl throws a bucket of water onto him, she inadvertently splashes the witch, causing her to melt away.
The guards gratefully give the girl the witch's broom, and the group returns to the wizard, but he tells them to come back the next day.
They protest, and the dog pulls back a curtain, revealing the "wizard" to be an ordinary man operating machinery.
When they confront him, he confesses to being a humbug, but "grants" the girl's friends' wishes by giving them tokens to confirm that they had the qualities they sought.
The wizard reveals that he, like the girl, is from her homeland and accidentally arrived in the realm in a hot air balloon.
He attempts to take her back home aboard it, but when the dog jumps out and the girl goes after him, the balloon lifts off with just the wizard aboard.
The good witch then reappears and tells the girl she always had the power to return home using the ruby slippers, but had to find that out for herself.
After sharing a tearful farewell with her friends, the girl clicks her heels three times and repeats, "There's no place like home."
The girl awakens in her own bed at home.
She recounts her adventures, but her aunt says that she just had a bad dream.
The girl tells the fortune teller and the farmhands that they were in the realm also, and they smile, humoring her.
As she hugs the dog, she gratefully exclaims, "Oh, auntie, there's no place like home!"
In 1927, a silent film actor and his co-star attend the premiere of their latest film, produced by a film studio.
On the red carpet, the actor tells the story of his rise to stardom, claiming to have grown up cultured and highly educated.
His words are contradicted by flashbacks showing his humble roots as a hoofer, vaudeville musician and stuntman alongside his childhood best friend and longtime collaborator, accompanied by a song.
The actor also expresses his admiration for the co-star, feeding rumors of a secret romance between them.
In reality, the rumors are a publicity stunt and the actor barely tolerates the co-star, although she believes that he loves her.
After the premiere, the actor is mobbed by fans and escapes by jumping into a passing car driven by a woman.
The woman reluctantly gives the actor a lift.
She claims to be a theatre actress and expresses disdain for film acting, particularly the actor's hammy performances.
The actor responds by mocking her acting aspirations, and they part on bad terms.
The actor arrives at the afterparty, where the studio's CEO
shows a demonstration of a talking picture, though his guests dismiss it as a fad.
A group of chorus girls then performs, the woman among them (a song).
Furious at the actor's teasing, the woman attempts to throw a cake at him, but he dodges it and it hits the co-star instead.
In the confusion, the woman runs away.
Three weeks later, the actor has searched unsuccessfully for the woman.
The friend tries to cheer the actor up (a song).
The co-star reveals that she had the woman fired, infuriating the actor.
The friend finds the woman working as an extra in another film from the studio (a song).
The woman admits to actually being a fan of the actor's, while the actor professes his love for her (a song).
When another studio releases its first talking picture and it is an enormous hit, the CEO
decides he has to convert the actor and co-star's next film into a talkie.

The film's preview screening is a failure due to multiple complications, including awkward microphone placements, the actor's uninspired improvising and the audio going out of synchronization.

Later that night, the woman and the friend suggest the film be turned into a musical (a song), and the friend, inspired by the film's synchronization error, suggests that the woman dub the co-star's voice.
The actor happily agrees, then takes the woman home and dances through her neighborhood in the rain (a song).
The actor and the friend pitch their idea to the CEO
changing the title of the film and adding a modern framing device (a song).

The actor helps the woman dub the co-star's lines (a song), but the co-star is tipped off by another actress.
When the co-star realizes that the actor and the woman are in love and learns that the CEO
intends to give the woman a screen credit for her dubbing, she gives interviews across town promoting her (non-existent) vocal talent.
A clause in the co-star's contract allows her to sue the studio for negative press, so the CEO
is forced to leave the woman uncredited and agree to the co-star's demand that the woman continue anonymously dubbing for her.
The premiere of the film is a success, but when the audience clamors for the co-star to sing live, the actor, the friend, and the CEO
tell her to lip sync into a microphone while the woman, concealed behind the curtain, sings into a second microphone.
While the co-star is "singing" (a song), the men raise the curtain, revealing the ruse.
The co-star and the woman both flee in embarrassment, but the actor has the audience stop the woman and proudly announces that she is "the real star of the picture" (a song).
